beats.lead: The company that turned down his job application ended up paying him billions.
beats.text: In 2009, Brian Acton applied for a job at Facebook and was rejected. He had already been turned down by Twitter too.
beats.note: He was an experienced engineer, not a novice: both companies passed on him within the same year.

beats.text: He tweeted about the Facebook rejection on 3 August 2009: 'Facebook turned me down. It was a great opportunity to connect with some fantastic people. Looking forward to life's next adventure.'
beats.note: His next adventure was already underway. Former Yahoo colleague Jan Koum had incorporated WhatsApp Inc. that February, and Acton joined him later that year.

beats.text: Acton helped raise 250,000 dollars in seed funding from five former Yahoo colleagues and was granted co-founder status once he came aboard.
beats.note: The money came from people who already trusted him from his Yahoo days, not from a venture pitch to strangers.

beats.context: roughly the value, in dollars, of the deal Facebook announced on 19 February 2014 to acquire WhatsApp, the company built by the man it had rejected for a job.

beats.text: The deal, split between cash, stock and restricted stock units, closed on 6 October 2014, eight months after the announcement.

beats.line: Rejected for a job in 2009. Paid billions for his company in 2014.
